claim: Dangerous Grounds is the crustal impactor province — attenuated/rifted continental crust (Steuer et al. 2012) detached from the South China conjugate margin — not a basin with an independent fill history.
Rifted DG crust continues SE beneath Neogene Borneo sediments at least halfway to the slope toe; Kinabalu partly stacked on it at depth (hypothesis, untested).
source: Arif ENTERPRISE relay 2026-09-30 (EVIDENCE-classed in source relay; GEOX holds it as hypothesis pending dip-line test)

claim: SCS spreading began ~33-32 Ma (C12; IODP Exp 349) and died ~16.9-15.5 Ma when DG jammed the NW Borneo trench (Clift et al. 2008); ~20.5 Ma collision bracket retained as alternative.

DG carbonate growth was partly supported by a flexural FOREBULGE shallow zone migrating from the Borneo-Palawan trough toward the DG (Steuer et al. 2014) — carbonate tops are time-transgressive environmental markers, not sequence boundaries.
